correctness.rationale: For char≠2, so4 split acts on k^2⊗k^2 as two commuting sl2 factors. Partial traces of X² force a vanishing tensor product, so every square-zero X lies in exactly one factor. Nonzero sl2 nilpotent centralizers are one-dimensional. The conic of nilpotent lines has q+1 rational points; inclusion-exclusion gives all tuple and product counts. In nonsplit Witt index one, skew-adjoint X has even rank while X²=0 forces totally isotropic image, hence X=0. Over an algebraic closure, nilpotent-line cones of dimension m+1 yield 2^r incomparable irreducible products Z_S, dimensions r+1 at S empty/full and r+2 otherwise. Frobenius swaps the two ideals in the nonsplit case. Exhaustive literal-matrix tests over F3, F5 and F7 passed; extension fields and geometric components are proved rather than experimentally enumerated.

value.rationale: The result identifies exactly where nonzero ordinary products arise among commuting square-zero orthogonal operators, gives all rational-point counts for arbitrary tuple length and both Witt types, and establishes a reduced geometric locus with 2^r components in two different dimensions. The contrast with equidimensional unrestricted nilpotent commuting pairs and the nonsplit zero-rational-point phenomenon despite positive-dimensional geometric components give substantive representation-theoretic and arithmetic-geometric motivation.
